problem: LLM-based VLN agents fall far short of VLN specialists. Zero-shot GPT-4 agents (NavGPT, MapGPT, DiscussNav) trail by about 40% SR on R2R because of lossy captioning and summarization and fragile prompting. LLMs fine-tuned on VLN data (LangNav, NavCoT, NaviLLM) still lag behind and also lose the LLM's general language ability, such as explaining decisions or communicating.
motivation: LLMs bring commonsense, free-form language understanding and the ability to explain navigation decisions to humans. Yet frozen LLMs understand spatial structure poorly and cannot model long navigation histories, and fine-tuning them on scarce embodied data is inefficient and turns them into black boxes. The authors therefore keep the LLM frozen as a visual-linguistic representation and reasoning generator, and hand action planning with history to a specialist topological-graph policy.
key_idea: Use the latent states of a frozen, navigation-reasoning-tuned InstructBLIP VLM (instruction-aware Q-former image tokens plus instruction tokens, encoded by the FlanT5 encoder) as input features to a DUET-style topological-graph policy. The VLM can still decode natural-language navigational reasoning.
insight: The gain comes from the representation, not from making the LLM decide. Removing the policy network and letting the frozen LLM act collapses val-unseen SR from 67.52 to 21.46. Swapping DUET's vision features to the same EVA-CLIP-g gives no gain (val-unseen SR 62→63), so the improvement is attributed to projecting vision into the LLM's language space via the Q-former. LLM latents are also more data-efficient: with 50% of R2R, NavGPT-2-XL gets 63.30 val-unseen SR vs 63.90 for DUET with 100%. Two further lessons: (1) encoder-decoder FlanT5 (full attention, strong at multiple choice) clearly beats larger decoder-only Vicuna (71.31 for FlanT5-XXL vs 53.77/48.28 for Vicuna-7B/13B), so model size alone does not help; (2) pretraining the Q-former on GPT-4V reasoning adds only marginally to SR (67.52 vs 66.75) and mainly serves to enable interpretable reasoning.
method: VLM backbone: InstructBLIP with frozen EVA-CLIP ViT-g/14 and frozen LLM (FlanT5-XL/XXL, Vicuna-7B/13B); each candidate view is encoded by a Q-former into 32 instruction-aware query tokens, then linearly projected into the LLM.

Navigation system prompt: structured prompt listing 'Candidate i, facing a_i degree, {direction}' with special tokens / wrapping image tokens and the instruction, so the LLM perceives multiple views with their headings.

Reasoning data and stage-1 tuning: GPT-4V generates single-step navigational reasoning for 10K random intermediate steps of R2R train trajectories, using heading-centred equirectangular panoramas; only the Q-former is instruction-tuned with the auto-regressive loss (200K steps, batch 8, AdamW, lr 1e-5 with cosine decay).

VLM latents as features: hidden states of image and instruction tokens come from the last encoder layer (FlanT5) or last decoder layer (Vicuna); an MLP merges each view's 32 image tokens into one token. Only the FlanT5 encoder is needed for navigation, giving 1.5B/5B models.

Graph-based policy (DUET global branch, no local branch): node embeddings are the average of view features plus direction and step embeddings, passed through self-attention; a cross-modal transformer cross-attends to the LLM-encoded instruction; graph-aware self-attention adds a pairwise-distance affinity matrix; a 2-layer FFN scores all graph nodes plus a stop node, visited nodes are masked, and the agent moves by shortest path, which enables backtracking.

Stage-2 policy learning: the VLM is frozen and only the policy is trained with behaviour cloning plus DAgger (pseudo labels from shortest paths on sampled partial graphs), with batch 2, lr 1e-5, on a single A100; the best model uses R2R plus PREVALENT synthetic data.

setting.backbone: InstructBLIP (frozen EVA-CLIP ViT-g/14 + Q-former tuned on reasoning data + frozen FlanT5-XL/XXL; Vicuna-7B/13B in ablation) feeding a DUET-global-branch graph policy trained from scratch on R2R
setting.model_size: 1.5B (FlanT5-XL encoder only) / 5B (FlanT5-XXL encoder only); Vicuna-7B/13B variants in ablation
setting.training_data: Stage 1: 10K GPT-4V-generated single-step navigational reasoning samples from R2R train (Q-former only). Stage 2: R2R train, plus PREVALENT synthetic instruction-trajectory augmentation for the best model (policy only). No VLN-specific pretraining.
setting.observation: RGB images of each navigable candidate view (one view per candidate node, not a full 36-view panorama) with relative heading angles, plus the instruction
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints; global selection among all nodes of the built topological graph (including stop), reached via shortest path, which allows backtracking
setting.simulator: Matterport3D simulator (R2R/RxR); Habitat-rendered HM3D images for the zero-shot HM3D test

numbers_note: Table 1 prints rounded integers for OSR/SR/SPL; Tables 3–5 give decimals for the R2R-only XL/XXL variants, and those decimals are used here. The text contains a typo that labels the 1.5B model 'FlanT5-XXL (1.5B)'. The HM3D evaluation is a custom set of 1000 trajectories sampled from ScaleVLN, not a standard benchmark. Other own variants not listed above: Vicuna-7B/13B (val-unseen SR 53.77/48.28); XL with 10%/50% R2R data (val-unseen SR 52.02/63.30); 'w/o policy model' (21.46); 'w/o pre-trained Q-former' (66.75). The human study (30 samples, 10 raters, 0–3 scale) scores NavGPT-2 FlanT5-XL at 1.66 accuracy / 1.93 informativeness / 1.78 rationality, vs GPT-4V at 2.31/2.95/2.34.
results: The best 5B model, NavGPT-2 FlanT5-XXL with PREVALENT data, reaches 74 SR / 61 SPL on R2R val-unseen and 72 SR / 60 SPL on test-unseen. It keeps the LLM frozen and still produces language reasoning. It beats every prior LLM-based agent: NaviLLM (Vicuna-7B, test 68 SR) by 4 SR, and the zero-shot GPT-4 agents by roughly 30+ SR on val-unseen. It also beats the architecture-matched DUET w/o local branch baseline by 5 SR / 2 SPL on test, and full DUET by 3 SR. It remains below DUET+ScaleVLN (77 SR test). In zero-shot transfer it beats DUET on RxR-EN (28.75 vs 25.07 SR) and by a much larger margin on HM3D (47.20 vs 25.60 SR).
limitations: The generated reasoning is single-step, based on local observation with no history in the VLM, and is not synchronized with the policy's actions, so its consistency and faithfulness are unverified; the VLM hallucinates objects and misjudges directions.

Communicative and interactive abilities (asking for help, following interventions) are shown only qualitatively and never evaluated; generated reasoning is rated clearly below GPT-4V in the human study.

Only discrete R2R-style nav-graph settings are tested, with no VLN-specific pretraining of the policy; the method still trails ScaleVLN-scale specialists, and decoder-only LLMs (Vicuna) perform much worse.
